summary.text: Clay Fuller is the Republican incumbent in Georgia's 14th District, which he has represented since April 2026. A former district attorney and Air Force judge advocate who was a White House Fellow in 2018-2019, he still serves in the Air National Guard. He won the April 7, 2026 special election runoff to succeed Marjorie Taylor Greene, and then the May 19 Republican primary.

paragraphs.text: Fuller was raised in the North Georgia mountains; according to his campaign survey, he is an eighth-generation North Georgian who lives in Dade County.
He was captain of the basketball team at Emory University, where he earned a bachelor's degree in English in 2004.

He went on to a Master of Public Administration from Cornell University (2006) and a J.D. from Southern Methodist University's Dedman School of Law (2009), and later earned a master's degree in military arts and sciences from the Air Command and Staff College (2020).
Fuller has served in the U.S. Air Force since 2009 and, according to his House biography, is a lieutenant colonel and Deputy Staff Judge Advocate in the Air National Guard.
He was deployed from May to November 2024 as legal advisor to the Combined Air Operations Center at Shaw Air Force Base and Al Udeid Air Base, Qatar.
In civilian life he served as District Attorney for the Lookout Mountain Judicial Circuit, a four-county circuit in northwest Georgia.
From 2018 to 2019 he was a White House Fellow, working in the Office of the Vice President and the Department of Defense, including on counter-terrorism matters.
According to his 2020 Ballotpedia survey, Fuller founded a company focused on bringing investment to small towns in north Georgia.
He ran for this seat in 2020 and lost in the Republican primary.
He won the special general runoff election for Georgia's 14th District on April 7, 2026, defeating Shawn Harris, and took office April 14, 2026, succeeding Marjorie Taylor Greene.
He won the May 19, 2026 regular Republican primary for the seat.
